testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You cannot drink alcohol within ____ before starting work.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle drivers cannot drink any alcohol within four hours before starting work.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Poorly balanced cargo makes a vehicle harder to handle. Distribute weight evenly when loading cargo.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums before each trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: The radiator cap:

options.text: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
Can be removed when the coolant is hot.
Should be cool to the touch under normal driving conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap while the system is hot. Hot steam and water can cause severe burns. Wait until the cap is cool to the touch before opening it.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle still has normal brakes without ABS. Brake as you normally would and have the ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.explanation: Sign the vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and either fixed or certified as not needing repair.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:

options.text: Increases a driver's ability to steer.

questions.explanation: Poorly balanced cargo makes driving unsafe. Distribute cargo weight evenly when loading your vehicle.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should have a maximum air loss of 4 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.explanation: Windows down in cold weather can be a sign of an impaired driver. Watch for this and other signs of unsafe driving.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These buildups can damage your brakes.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: Containerized loads are used:

options.text: When the cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When the cargo has been or will be transported by train.
When the cargo is a liquid.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight travels by rail or ship. The containers are sealed and cannot be inspected. The driver must make sure the containers do not exceed legal weight limits.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. This reduces the need for sudden speed or direction changes and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: Violation points for major violations stay on a driving record for:
questions.explanation: Points for major violations while driving a commercial vehicle or as a CDL holder stay on your record for 55 years.

questions.question: When doing a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull forward directly into the parking space.
Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parallel parking space on your left, drive past it first. Then back up into the space, keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: While going downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your vehicle reaches 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: If you cannot tell if the road is icy, you should:

options.text: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy but are not sure, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely icy.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when brakes are hot after a steep descent. Let them cool first to avoid brake damage.

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stopped position, you should:
questions.explanation: To prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the instrument panel.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look is when a driver opens the door, leaves their seat, and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you may use only one look. During other exercises, you may use up to two looks.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is only on one part of your vehicle, you still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both could damage your brakes.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving a vehicle to harm or assault others
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving a vehicle to harm or assault others
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is driving in a reckless or careless way.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you slowly apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights to show when ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS vehicles have yellow warning lights. They alert you when the braking system is not working. Find the warning light in your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: Talking on a cell phone while driving removes about ____ of a person's focus from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous. It takes away about 39 percent of your mental focus from driving.

questions.question: If turning to avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should not brake because it may lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake because it may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while making a quick turn. Braking during a sharp turn can lock your wheels and cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip:

options.text: No part of your vehicle should be visible in any mirror.
Some part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. This helps you judge where other objects are around you.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, you should shift into a lower gear:

options.text: After you have started the hill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before starting a downhill grade. Gravity will make your vehicle speed up going downhill.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop your vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Driving with hanging meat in a trailer can be challenging because:

options.text: It is not recommended during summer.
The load sits high and is unstable.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load sits high and is unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity. The meat swinging can also affect how you control the vehicle. Drive carefully with this type of load.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight hill.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle has trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailers are straight. Check your mirrors before every trip.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down hard and release. If it returns slowly, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down hard and release. If the brakes squeak, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times. Then press it down hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake problem.

questions.question: Tires not on the front of a commercial motor vehicle must have a tread depth of at least ____.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have 4/32 of an inch tread depth. All other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch tread depth.

questions.question: A ramp's posted speed limit:

options.text: May be too fast for large commercial motor vehicles.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for large commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Ramp speed limits are set for regular cars. Large or heavy commercial vehicles often need to go slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires the driver to have a CDL?
questions.explanation: Military vehicles, emergency vehicles, and farm equipment do not require a CDL. However, a school bus driver must have a CDL.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used with caution because:

options.text: Drivers may not see flares in sunny weather.

questions.explanation: Flares can ignite spilled fuel and cause fires. Use flares carefully after an accident.

questions.question: If you brake on dry pavement while traveling at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when brakes are applied.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means both systems are leaking.
May not affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction you want to go.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of your turn. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse your steering direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended:

options.text: You can get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.
You cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.
Your commercial driver license will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: The maximum height of a load is:
questions.explanation: In California, the maximum height for a vehicle and load is 14 feet, measured from the road surface. Some exceptions apply to farm equipment and double-deck buses.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.

questions.explanation: If air pressure becomes too low, air brakes may stop working. Pressing and releasing the brake pedal repeatedly can cause air to leak faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction of the turn.
Look in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. If a driver does not signal, their body movements may show they are planning to turn.

questions.question: One way to prevent drowsiness while driving is to:

options.text: Get enough sleep the night before the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before the trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before driving. Other ways to prevent drowsiness include having a passenger, scheduling trips during times you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise can also help you stay alert.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Yawning a lot or rubbing your eyes

questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, difficulty keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum air leak for a single vehicle with air brakes is:
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leak rate during an applied leakage test is 3 psi in one minute.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail while driving downhill, first look for an escape ramp. If no ramp is available, find another place to stop, such as an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.
